title: Bacs Direct Debit Submission File Corruption — Incorrect Character Encoding

content.summary: The Bacs Direct Debit submission file for 2024-09-03 was rejected by the Bacs central system due to character encoding corruption introduced by a library upgrade. 68,000 direct debit mandates were not processed, requiring next-day resubmission.

timeline.event: Bacs submission window opens; bacs-submission-service begins generating submission file
Submission file (68,000 records) transmitted to Bacs central infrastructure
Bacs returns NACK: 'Invalid character in name field — non-ASCII bytes detected'
P1 declared; engineering team begins investigating encoding issue
Root cause identified: file-writer library upgraded from v4.1 to v5.0 uses UTF-8 output; Bacs requires ASCII
Hotfix deployed with explicit ASCII encoding and character transliteration
Corrected file transmitted; Bacs confirms receipt for next-day processing

content.root_cause: The bacs-submission-service was upgraded to use file-writer v5.0, which changed the default output encoding from ASCII to UTF-8. The Bacs AUDDIS file format specification requires pure ASCII encoding. Customer name fields containing accented characters (e.g., é, ñ, ü) were written as multi-byte UTF-8 sequences, causing the file to fail Bacs validation. The v5.0 upgrade did not flag the encoding change in its breaking changes section.
contributing_factors: Bacs file format specification not included in automated test assertions
Library upgrade notes not reviewed by payments team (fourth certificate/encoding pattern incident in 2024)
No pre-submission file validation against Bacs AUDDIS schema

impact.customer_impact: 68,000 customers' direct debits collected one day late
impact.financial_impact: Potential late payment charges for some customers

immediate: Hotfix file-writer encoding to ASCII with transliteration fallback
Retransmit corrected file within Bacs cut-off window
short_term: Add Bacs AUDDIS schema validation as pre-submission gate (JIRA PAY-9400)
Add encoding assertion tests for all payment scheme file generators (JIRA PAY-9401)
Audit all payment file generators for encoding compliance (JIRA PAY-9402)
long_term: Implement payment scheme file format test suite covering all active schemes (Bacs, CHAPS, FPS)
Automate library upgrade impact analysis for payment-critical services
Add Bacs file validation tool to development environment
